Редкий симулятор выживания предлагает своему посетителю что-либо кроме самого выживания. Задачи в играх такого плана довольно просты. Набить брюхо, выспаться, чтобы найти чем набить брюхо перед следующей спячкой. Знакомство с большинством из них рано или поздно ставит перед выбором – чем себя занять? Либо построить красивый дом, либо водрузить на крышу лачуги акулу, либо вырезать всех мирных игроков, которые строят что-то вокруг, а затем наслаждаться воплями ограбленных и обездоленных вашими загребущими руками, в том случае, если симулятор выживания предполагает избиение невинных.
Приобретая «Salt» я думал, что это еще один такой симулятор. Что я научусь делать мечи и кирки, пробурю пару ходов, построю себе землянку и буду жить подобно медведю – набивая брюхо и впадая в сезонную спячку. Я ошибался. Точно также я ошибся, когда глядя на скриншоты подумал - «вероятно, игру делал программист». Ошибки уже давно вошли в привычку, ибо вкус безнадежно испорчен клонами одной и той же игровой механики «найди десяток бананов и собери пистолет». Целый сегмент индустрии эксплуатирует жанр «выживания» точно также как до этого эксплуатировали казуальные игры класса «найди пять бананов».
Однако оставим стручки стручкоедам. Оказавшись в игре, я резво пробежал по острову и собрал нехитрую снедь, которой оказалось достаточно, чтобы собрать утлый плот с небольшим парусом, на котором я незамедлительно отправился в плаванье. Начнем его и мы с вами, и проплывем по перечислению того, что дает эта игра в отличие от других подобных ей.
Море? Море. Оно волнуется и перекатывается. Есть высота волн, и движение судна по ним. Это выгодно отличает «Salt» от «Stranded Deep» (как наиболее близкий по тематике) где движение происходит по одной плоскости. У вашего судна есть руль, который позволяет управлять кораблем. Вы можете передвигаться по плоту или судну во время движения не опасаясь, что каким-либо багом вас сметет прочь.
Сойдя на землю, вы можете невзначай выяснить, что флора и фауна на разных островах различаются. Что на островах есть сундуки, пираты, капища и другие секреты. Что на них, как ни странно есть другие люди, и не все из них норовят выпустить вам кишки. О да, здесь можно поболтать и получить квесты. Что второй лук или еще один меч, что вы нашли это не такой же объект, и что у него есть свойства. Что описаны лишь базовые элементы крафта, а остальные вы найдете сами… в книгах. Недурно, не правда ли? Кто бы ожидал этого от маленькой и цветастой игры.
И вот я уже несусь между островами осмысленно, ведомый выданным мне заданием. Попутно обнаруживаю разбитый корабль, который можно починить, в трюме «компас, что не указывает на север». Книги, в которых полностью или частично описаны предметы, которые я могу собрать. Описаны не как список предметов, которые дадут другой предмет. Нет. Это настоящие книжки. Дневники пиратов. Схемы написанные кем-то. Мемуары скитальцев. Каждый остров может таить в себе секрет. Каждый остров может и будет отличаться. Каждый остров не будет спрайтом на горизонте как в «Stranded Deep», который затем заменится на совершенно другой остров, делая навигацию не то чтобы не нужной, но невозможной. Нет. Здесь всё по-честному – какой остров увидел, такой формы он и будет когда вы подплывете. Это позволит вам плыть на глазок. По памяти. Ну а если глазок хромоват – существует секстант. Да и блокнот на столе, с ручкой и координатами в нем никто не отменял.
Графика, когда вы уже в игре, не кажется работой программиста. Это некий минимализм. На пределе. Он уместен. Он к месту. Он самодостаточен.
Вы когда-нибудь охотились в симуляторах выживания? Чаще зверь это невероятно тупая тушка, которая стоит на месте и ожидает, когда её превратят в гамбургер. Куда реже это тушка, которая делает вид что удирает, но будучи медленной от рождения всё равно попадает к вам на обед. Ещё реже вам приходиться гоняться за дичью, загоняя её и думая с какой стороны напасть так чтобы зверь не ушел. Это тот самый редкий случай.
Симулятор... симулятор выживания? О чем это он? И верно. О чем это я? Все мы знаем, что частенько разработчики добавляют своему проекту разные теги. Adventure, или RPG. Даже если игра содержит лишь их куцые элементы. Эта игра ещё не рпг, но стремится к этому. И это абсолютно точно - приключение. Не в поисках банки тушенки. Не в поисках кого бы ограбить. Нет. Это настоящая игра про пиратов, море и клады.

Hitman: Absolution marks the final nail in the coffin for a once promising franchise; the Hitman: Codename 47.
The game's earliest titles, like Codename 47, and Silent Assassin, were both revolutionary games in the 'free roam assassin' genre, where you had multiple access methods, several scenarios to take out your target with, and a freedom to choose whether to go in hot and deadly and go for the Mass Murderer title, or go in silent and unnoticed and get Silent Assassin. It was up to you, and it had never been done before. The Hitman Franchise was once a blaring success, and many games were sold.
However...As what happens with most developpers who see dollar signs(And you can't blame them, they're only human...Greed comes naturally to us once we taste immeasurable success...We want more). They got off the trails, gave up their outside-the-box thinking strategy, and started to give up on what made Hitman special, and slowly turned it into a shooter. Blood Money was on the verge, with some few points that made it worth buying, but Hitman:Absolution marks the fall of once beautiful franchise.
The game.Is.Complete.and utter.TRASH!
THe once all important Stealth design has been pretty much ignored...Putting on a disguise doesn't really help you with remaining undetected much, as you are fully dependant on your 'Instincts' which is pretty much nothing more than a bar which is represented in a similar fashion to Fantasy games' Mana Pool. It fills when you complete objectives or make tactically accurate moves, and gets drained when you use it...And it is 110% required to use it to slip past guards...Even with a disguise on! I actually found that in more cases than not, it was more beneficial to simply NOT take a disguise, and stay in your suit and tie as long as possible, cause for some reason, guards found a guy in a Mechanic's outfit, outside a mechanic's shop, suspicious enough to shoot at. More so, than a bald ominous guy in a black suit, crouching behind a car...Completely normal Saturday wierdness, right guys?
The 'Going in loud' is also heavily recommended, and it is obvious in just how many tools you're given to kill lots and lots of people...Such as Point Shooting...Use up a chunk of Instinct per target, a total of 4, which you mark, and then hit the Execute key. 47 stands up, and instantly, without any effort, shoots all 4 enemies.
Furthermore...In each mission you have the oppertunity to 'discover' new weapons...Such as revolvers, uzi's m4's, sniper rifles, shotguns, baseballbats, crowbars, crossbows etc. etc. lots of full automatic weapons to really paint an entire map read in blood. Now all this would be cool...If it actually benefitted you...Because for some strange reason, the developpers decided to provide all of these ways to kill people, and all of these cool full automatic weapons to collect, and KEEP THE SILENT ASSASSIN FAVORING SCOREBOARD!...
This means that you will score 'more' points if you IGNORE all of these cool new killing methods/weapons, and go with old school Hitman style gameplay, killing as few people as possible except the target, and getting out undetected, most of the time doing so without having fired a single shot...But if you decide to use these amazing modern-hitman bonus kill methods, you actually LOSE points, and it is completely impossible to go into a Hitman Absolution game, and complete a mission by shooting everything, and getting out with a + sided score count...It will ALWAYS, ALWAYS result in a NEGATIVE scoring if you go in loud...So you are in fact punished for using these new features in Absolution.
The developpers had NO IDEA where they wanted to go with this game...They finally got impatient, took a huge overdose of Fokitol, and released the game with an absolutely BROKEN stealth system, a COMPLETELY unfair scoring system, and a COMPLETELY POINTLESS new set of killing styles that you get PUNISHED for using...
NOT recommended. Jesus Christ guys, let the Hitman franchise die with its dignity intact, stop trying to squeeze the last little bit of green out of its husked corpse already.

Well the graphics are shiny, but that's about it. It's a decent stealth sneaking game and has some interesting level design at times, but it's plagued with many many issues. For instance, how on earth does it make sense that me sniping a guy through a window 200 yards away alone in a room makes my police disguise worthless? Yet, if I change into civ clothes in the very same room, cops will rush in and wander around me in circles wondering where the killer went. Not only is this insane abuse, it's also incredibly stupid. The story is alright, you kind of need to be invested in the Hitman storyline to really appreciate it. It's nothing special.
The worst thing about the game is by far is just all the little flaws. If I walk by a window ledge and yank some guy out and drop him 10 stories while he was in a room with a dozen people, no one will care. Similarly, if I go to a maid and smash her face in with a fire extinguisher, I get a massive point drop for killing a civ. But if I choke her til she's unconcious, drag her to a window and drop her several floors to her death never to be seen again, I get my points back? It's easy to go on and on about all these details and it really hurts the overall experience of the game.
If you're really looking for a stealth game, I suppose you could do worse, but this isn't the shining star of the hitman series by any means.

To put this review into context, a small info from my end: i am a long time smash player and still play Smash 4 on a daily basis but soly 1vs1 for glory. So i am focused on the competitive spectrum of smash play.
Rivals of Aether is exactly that, a "smashlike" with laser focus on competitive 1vs1 play.
This shows in many aspects of the game:
1.) There is no blocking. This might sound harsh but it is the right thing todo, since blocking has always been a flawed mechanic in smash. To compensate you get a pary. Just press the button at the right moment when an enemy is about to hit you and you get a few frames of invincibility to counter your enemies moves.
2.) No ledge grabbing. The ledge grabbing has always been a special part of smash games, but it also slowed the games down and in some matchups lead to a VERY simplistic interpretation of rock, paper, scissors. In RoA you cant grab the ledge but any character can wall jump and do his recovery afterwards. This results in a much faster and skill based meta for of stage recovery/edge guarding.
3.) Easy wave dashing. Wave dashing is back and easier then ever. Just press a direction and the pary button + jump at the same time.
4.) very distinct characters. even though there are only 6 characters in the game so far, all of them are very unique and each matchup playes completely different.
Even though this is early access the game is  VERY enjoyable and the netcode is allready better then in smash 4.
So do yourself a favour and pick this one up asap.

As interesting as the description of the game makes it out ot be, I can't currently recommend this came for other individuals to play.
It is currently in a very unfinished and unpolished state. While it is 'functional' and they player is able to engage with the gameplay, it feel very rough around the edges. The entire game is left up to you to discover how it works and why things do what they do. While this is desirable at some points, this game does not implement this aspect in a good way.
I feel as though Space Radiance could be a good game and I really like what it tried to implement, it just isn't yet finished. Hopefully the developer will keep at it and make the interface and gameplay a bit more smooth and presentable for the final audience.
The first few levels only allow the player to use one 'form' yet there are multiple green gases to cover. While I understand the strategy and intent behind this (preventing the player from essentially just walling up and winning) there are times that this makes the level essentially unwinable. The flying beams have seemingly random velocites when they enter the screen and there are often times, such as the case in level three, where the beam moves too fast to click and move your 'form.'
I don't see much fun in a game that you can really win at when that is not the intentional goal. I would love to be able to do longer term levels where I could 'train up' and then build a better protection 'form' to use in future defenses. The game plays a bit like this currently but it is a lot of trial and error, and a lot of restarting levels simply because you were faced with an unbeatable challenge.
I'm wating for the next big update to move this game in a new and improved direction, but until then I think the best bet is to pass on it or find it in a bundle.

I am going to start this review by saying I wish steam had something other than yes or no. Right now I have to leave it at a no. I really wanted to like this game, in fact I DID like this game for about the first two weeks. Then when the honeymoon period ended and what I thought was a pretty good looking wife turned out to be shallow and Vapid and kind of annoying.
So I should I should start with the Positives.
-Taming- If you can see it in the world Odds are you can tame it and ride it or have it as a pet. This includes pretty much most bosses as well.
-Graphics- This is quite a pretty game. Not stunning however for an MMO, full settings look quite nice and it seems to scale to various machines and at the basics it runs pretty well.
I really thought that I would have more Positives.
NEGATIVES
-Taming- So yeah this is on here twice because while you CAN tame everything in the world. The grind to acquire many of those seals needed to tame them can be quite daunting. Throw into that the fact that you have a chance to fail at taming which consumes the mark which means you have to start over. Then add in the fact that you often need to tame multiples in order to create a mark in order to tame something stronger. If this appeals to you, rock on, this is the game for you.
-Mounted Combat!!!- Right how can a game that is about riding mounts suck at mounted combat. I don't know but they managed it. Activated abilities get interupted by an autoattack that you cannot turn off. Targetting can be quite hit or miss. The range that you fight at is so short (under 20 meters) And enemies hit hard. Throw into that the Health sponges many things are in this game and you end up in a poorly executed circle strafe fest.
-Population- There is pretty much none. Granted I am on the smallest server but, you will notice long stretches of time that you go without seeing another person playing the game. I started up the game and right off the bat it caps you at 60 FPS. Unfortunately, the graphics troubles weren't over. This game is very poorly optimized despite how long it has been out. If you end up buying the game (get it on sale) there is a user guide to tweak the graphics options to fix all the problems.
Once I finally got into the game I was behind the wheel of a ship and I couldn't move at all. I  wasn't sure what was going on so I waited for a bit and eventually got killed and the game reset me to retry the beginning. This time, I could move but my character was glitched into the belly of the ship. But at least I could move! However, I wasn't able to get out of this glitch and unable to pull up any type of menu so I had to kill the game from task manager and retry again. As it turns out the third times the charm! The game loaded up and there I was behind the wheel... underwater... Rushing up toward the surface of the water I piloted the ship like something out of Pirates of the Carribean. The ship breached like a whale landing firmly on the stormy waves and I began the game. All the ships in this first sequence also chose to come from Davy Jones Locker so I guess that's how we are playing this one. This also happened through out the game at random times.
All the graphical issues aside, you will have to put up with Uplay. And if you live somewhere with spotty internet just be aware you will need to be online to play this even in single player. For all of these reasons above I cannot recommend this game. Moving on to the actual gameplay though:
First don't expect an Assassin's Creed game. That's not what this really is. It's more like Pirate Simulator build on the Assassin's Creed engine if you will. And it's absolutely fantastic! It has everything you can think of when it comes to Pirate Simulator, ships, upgrades, crew, battles, forts, swinging from ropes, your very own pirate fleet, treasure maps. I had a blast being a pirate.
The story wasn't bad, and on its own quite good. But if you played all the other games and know their stories then this one will kinda fall flat on its face.
The environment was incredible. Towns and the jungle were so much fun to play in. However, the combat is extremely repetetive and gets to be a chore very quickly. If you are the type of player to want to rambo in swords drawn cutting people down you won't have a good time. This game is about using the environment and getting the quiet kill. I really enjoyed this aspect of it and felt like the designers put a lot of thought into how all these elements came together to make the rogue like experience trully expetional.
I have no doubt in my mind that this could have been an absolutely amazing game. It was fantastic, but I don't think it'll be remembered for instance like Skyrim. I think it really could have though, with a little more focus on the story and sorting out the Uplay/bugs I think this game could have been incredible. Not to say that those things can't be fixed, but I think that ship has sailed.

Civ BE is a solid addition to the Civilization series.   There are parts of this game that are brand new to the series that I love.   It does appear that they pushed it out a little fast with a few areas that could be more polished, but overall I love it.
To be fair, I'm a long-time Civ fanboy.  I pre-ordered and have counted down the days.   The game gets a "meets expectations" for me and thats saying alot as my expectations were high.   I made sure not to compare the game too much to Civ5 in its current state with all add-ons as thats hardly fair.  However,  I am juding this as a Civilization game and thats a pretty high benchmark.
Quick pro's and cons:
CONS:
- Trade Route Hell - As much as I like the new trade system I find it very difficult to list it as a con, but having to re-enable trade routes over and over his heinous.   For the love of all that is fun PLEASE give the option on the (hidden) trade route screen (F10) to click a "repeat this route and leave me the F* alone".   That "feature" alone makes late game tedious beyond belief.
- Easy AI on lower difficulties - Ok... so they are dumb.  Super dumb.  Unless you play on a mid-high level you may as well snooze due to the lack of aggression.  I've won a couple of games (on large maps) without ever being at war.  Ever.  On higher difficulties its more aggressive but seems to have some quirks that need worked out... nothing game busting though.
- Lack of "immersion" - SMAC is one of my top-five all time favorite games.  One of the greatest things about it was the immersion.   I can still hear Lady Deidre Sky talking about postponing her time in the vats.   When Firaxis said this was not a Alpha Centauri, but was the spiritual predecesor... I thought they meant in lines of immersion.   It doesn't have to be the same story, but make me feel a part of it.    I've researched everything on the tech tree a dozen times now... some of them mean nothing to me.   No voiceover talking about tensile strength etc helping me to understand what it is.  Just a quick popup (and I do read them) and meh.   This should be fixed.  Firaxis missed a great opportunity here.
- Wonders.   Somewhere in Firaxis there has to be someone going "Yeah... people are going to hate the decisions the lead designers made here".   They are blah.  Not much more powerful than standard buildings, no cutscenes, and in most cases I don't even know what the thing I just built does and I read everything!   WTH does a Bytegeist do?
- Pick a path! - This maybe the thing I like the least.   You can follow multiple seemingly-contradictory paths at the same time in the affinities.   Nothing is to keep you from being a nature-loving, cyborg, humanist.  Its dumb.  Really makes me feel far less immersed.   At the very least it is balanced.  If you DO decide to do this you will find it difficult to win in an evenly matched game.   Non-violent victory conditions are at the higher ranks of affinities and the violent player would be eaten alive by higher-tier units available to a specialist.   However... if you pull ahead from the other players and have reached the required affinity level to start a non-violent victory condition - you can suddenly become very tri-polar in nature.
PROS:
- Graphics and Sound -  Amazing.  The music is great and really sets the stage.  The graphics are top-notch.  I love how the cities and units start to look like your affinity.  (minus the silly multi-affinity crap)
- Starting conditions - new feature to CIVs and I love it.   You can choose citizen type, landing conditions as well as faction.  You can customize your abilities to match your play style.   Fantastic.
- Trade routes - They are great.  I am addicted to getting and keeping as many as I can.   You really have to decide here how to go.   Trade routes to your own cities promote growth and industry while routes to foreign cities promote wealth and sceince for both of you.  That can be dangerous because you are giving a huge boost to your trade partner as well.    The strategic use of trade routes and ability to grow early cities super fast or increase your science output massively is really cool.  Just see my complaint above.
- Tech web - Great idea.  Non-linear and balanced near the outsides.  Rewards heavy investment one direction quite well.   "primary" techs each have techs under them, and that is where you will find most of your affinity points.  Each player and affinity will crawl the tech tree differently leading to drastically different play styles, needs, and strengths.
- City cap and sprawl - I see this being listed as a negative, but I really like the balance.  You can't drop cities like crazy without taking a heavy penalty to health.   You can either assume that penalty and push on anyways, or limit yourself to how many cities your health cap can provide.  If you choose to push hard on the tech tree for health you will NOT get affinity points, or wonder techs, etc.   Its a choice.   I have never had much trouble spreading out at a decent rate.  Start with a core of 3-4 and then push techs/affinities to give yourself more.  If you are a warmonger who focuses on military you likely wont get above those 3-4 without conquering.
- City building bonuses - Wow.  Didn't see this one coming.   When you build your first set of a certain type of building you are presented with a question/question.   You have one of two routes you can take each building and that bonus will last for the rest of the game.  Do you want your Earth Relic to be free or give more culture?   Free will give you a nice boost early on your tight cash, but that culture will start pumping out culture.   This is another way for civilizations to specialize.   I do really like the concept and execution.
- Virtues - Spend that culture on Virtue bonuses.  Unlike CivV they have added a bit more strategy and flexibility here.   Instead of being "pick one and finish it" there are actually benefits for getting multiple unrelated Tier 1 virtues.  Or if you are the type to stick to it you get bonuses for finished an area.   I see this being a huge plus as not all players that are doing an affinity/virtue combination are going to be the same.   I find myself liking certain builds (think specs) when playing one way or another.   Great balance and lots of fun to explore.
- Native life - Yeah... WAY better than barbarians.  Its a real threat.  It almost makes up for the complete lack of a threat from the AI early on.  Early in the game those advanced native units are nasty.   Harmony affinity receives a nice boost here due to being able to keep passive/neutral with them for so long.
- Balance and strategy - I would have not said this for the first 10-20 hours of play, but there is QUITE a bit under to the hood here.   In addition to Faction bonuses you have starting conditions.  Those two things will be working together before you set foot on the planet.  Once landed you will find that you have to make choices on city locations for resources (each affinity needs a certain type of resource!), affinity selection, city building bonuses, virtue strategy based on available resources nearby, etc.    To be successful at higher difficulties it pays to specialize based on available resources.  Try to befriend AI's with similar affinities as that bonus is very strong.
I'm iffy on multiplayer (buggy), covert ops, and quests (clunky, but great concept)
All in all this is a great game.  It surely should have been polished a bit more before being released, but I really like it in its current state.   I'm unwilling to compare it to a fully-exansion-packed Civ V as that seems unreasonable, but compared to all other games in the category out of the box its a solid performer.    I'm having a blast.  Now... back to my next game.  ;)

I thought I had learned my lesson about pre-ordering a game with Sim City and Alien Colonial Marines. Nope, when Civ Beyond Earth was first announced I was over the moon and immediately hit the Pre-order button when it was available. After all, Firaxis performed miracles with Alpha Centauri and its follow-up expansion Alien Crossfire which became my favorite games of all time, or at least up to now. I still keep SMAC/AXfire installed on current machines to play. Yes, I was hoping Beyond Earth was going to be Alpha Centauri 2. Well it certainly isn't. My first impression of Beyond Earth has to do with the graphics. I know a Civ game is all about the gameplay but for this day and age I was really hoping for gorgeous graphics with detailed planets, maps, and units. Instead everything is rather drab with no definition and extremely grey-scaled. The gameplay itself resides on the boring side and is marred with a confusing interface and non-intuitive mouse clicking, and inexcusable spelling/grammatical errors. I am really hoping there are updates to bring Beyond Earth to life and make it the interstellar TBS that it should have been (and hyped up to be if you followed the devs on Facebook & Twitter).
And this folks is the reason I am RECOMMENDING Beyond Earth. If the game is purchased and supported enough and the resulting negative reviews continue to escalate then the game improvements will happen more quickly when Firaxis takes notice and takes their Civ fans seriously.

So i bought this game on starting day.
First off it i was very excited about it...then a few hours later i realised my expectations were misplaced. A week later i realised that this game is nothing like we had hoped for or what was announced.
Secondly with this game, all were eager to try out multiplayer. Apparantly Firaxis/2k still did not manage to make a game that can RUN well if one wants to play multi. The game constantly crashes, freezes, basicly shows every bug and mess civ 5 used to show. Not just that they left a huge problem with 1920*1080 resolution. Most folks cant even play it on full screen.
The bad thing is 3 days later came a patch for civ 5 with this game, makeing the non playable multiplayer bugs reapper, so now we have both games with multiplayer bugs.  (Though with civ 5 multiplayer dual is playable, with beyond earth about 4 players)
Thirdly. Basicly the new affinity and virtue system is a joke. Why? Because growth is the only one worth to take as a virtue, and purity as an affinity. By the time you would get some bonuses from any other, you are dead. Dominated to be precise by the purity player.
Let me elaborate on this:
-Virtue: Growth: OP.Basicly gives you everything you need to start off well. Free worker, free colonist, worker speed enhanced, and on tier 2 all your new colonists start with +2 population. (Aka 3!) not to mention they evolve 50% faster into colonies from outposts, oh and you get a one time bonus of 7! health on tier 2. Which makes you able to have 4 colonies quite easily before round 50. No other tier allows you that. Tried with a number of virtues none can get as usefull like this. The science virtue is basicly a joke, since by the time you could normally have 4 colonies with health buildings or improvements you are too far behind. Both population both science and both money wise. (not to mention affinity)
-Affinity: Purity: OP. Why? Firstly your explorer becomes untouchable by aliens, you can use it to defend everything. Because early in the game it is the aliens that bother you. You escort your colonies workers whatever with it. The three bonus modules from growth just make the meven more OP! Secondly this is the only affinity that receives a +2 health building quite early in the game.Requirement is purity 2. Gene Garden. Thereafter level 4 gets you the first early game affinity special unit the Battlesuit, it is by itself allrey more powerfull then any of the other affinites, not to mention that it requires titanium only. Which is a tier 1 tech. Harmony and Supremacy both require tier 3/4 techs...Biomass  and Firaxite. WHICH ARE NOT STRATEGIC RESOURCES. So even if there is strategic balance turned on you will msot likely have neither of them. End of story. (The thing is harmonies first bonus just reduces their agression towards you, WHICH SEEMS TO BE COMPLETELY random, i have not attacked any aliens since game start then the moment they can they kill your marines that guard a worker or a colonist. Throwing you further back. Explorer purity affinity-> safety line)
So basicly the game is won by the guy who gets the first purity point for free, explores everything gets all the expeditions from the three bonus modules of the growth. Then just walks aroun with his explorers around between aliens. And gets battlesuits up before turn 90 and dominates. End of story.
Also comparing all the other affinity bonuses to Purity ones...well they are a joke. (Not to mention their early tech special buildings since it will allways be health you need...nothing else but health and the strategic resource which you will NOT GET FROM ANY OF THEIR SPECIAL BUILDINGS!)
So this game is broken in so many ways, i do not encourage anyone to buy it at full price. Perhaps if there is a sale 15 dollars at best it is worth. I am unsure if they even tested this game...
So another huge disappointment. A game that gave a huge hype and as we are getting used to it for nothing. So i recommend you not to buy it.

I obtained this videogame through a giveway from the publisher, and frankly I'm not only flabbergasted, I'm pleased: Blockstorm is a lovely, simplistic videogame. The gameplay mechanics strongly remind me of those found in "Counter-Strike", and combined with an art style similar to "Minecraft", the end mixture turns out to be a very enjoyable, fairly polished product that you can crack anytime alone or with friends and have fun.
The overall presentation was quite exquisite. The interface is generally well organized, clean and sleek-looking, and has multiple options you can de/activate and switch at will. I'm not impressed with the background music, but I'm not disappointed either: It captures the game's pace effectively, but certain pieces and riffs can be rather bleak or unglamorous. No complaints regarding that area, I prefer listening to music over silence, but in my opinion it leaves room for improvement. For those who are not fond of it, fortunately a checkmark in the settings exists to disable these tracks from playing.
The game features 6 gameplay modes, the classic "Deathmatch" and "Team Deathmatch", "Assault", "Capture The Flag", "Castle Battle" and "Hunt". Further information and details can be found in the videogame's
. I figured it is rather fleshed-out, so I do not need to paste the context here.
The game demonstrates a vast array of weapons you can choose from, but be careful about which ones you pick, because in turn it incorporates a "weight" system, and your mobility changes accordingly to the density of your equipment. You can aim down the sights of each weapon to boost your accuracy, like in other shooters. The shooting component is gratifying, but the sound effects are generally dull and lack in vigorousness.
The environment is merely built using destructible blocks, which you can smash using any kind of weapon, or blast them with explosives for extra carnage. You're also given the tools to dig or place new blocks and unleash your imagination, or alternatively, on the battlefield, to build cover, short paths, sniping spots etc.
The community overall gave me a positive view. From my experience, nobody used offensive language against other players and/or were generally toxic. On the contrary, I met new pretty cool people through this game who I still talk to outside of the game. I didn't notice any hackers or cheaters in my personal play-through, which is a plus for the multiplayer experience.
The game itself is highly customizable and features a built-in editor which allows you to produce new weapon skins, character models and maps, that you can publicize and share with your friends.
Overall, I personally think this game can be very fun and I recommend it for several scenarios, such as when you'd simply like to frag other opponents, if you're feeling creative, and lastly, if you ran out of other games to play. I give it an 8/10.

This is a great game.
Dare I say greatest game I've played so far this year? and yes, I've played Shadow of Mordor.
This survival strategy/simulation game put you in the roles of multiple civilian trapped in a war.
It's a new look on war-related game and 11bits studios pull it off gloriously.
With each day pass, switching between base management by day and scavenging missions by night, you'll grow attached to the characters under your care more and more and never want to see anyone of them dies.
The game has great atmospheres and a good challenge curve by keep throwing more difficult tasks/hindrances your way the longer your group stay alive.
In this war-torn city, You will get to choose to be a good group of people who help anyone in trouble or be an evil force that take from other people. The random events that happen during the gameplay are often very challenging to your decision making skill with nice, satisfying payoff.
Let me leave you with one random event that happened on one of my scavenging mission:
My guy was at a ruined of a supermarket. The description of the place said the place was under military control and very dangerous(this was my first time doing a "danger" scavenging mission). I went in, looked through the first floor entrance, saw this soldier talking to a female civillian looking for food. His raunchy dialog clearly showed that something bad is about to happen, but he has an assault rifle on him and all my guy got was a shovel that was about to break. So, I chose to avoid them and went up to the 2nd floor keep looking for useful resources, all the while still hearing the conversation down below played out.
Finally, the soldier started to hit the woman and I just can't have it anymore (I've never go up against enemy with guns before) So I switch mode to combat(I accidently did this once before and cause a big mess in a church :( ) with the shovel in hand, my guy slam through the door and bash the soldier in the back of the head! He staggered and fell and I went in for the kill. The woman was screaming and ran away and I thought that was it. I got some nice equipments from the soldier and went back to the base. The other characters in the house was praising my guy for his heroic action, which felt nice.
The next night I went back to the place again to find another female scavenger in the area. At first, I tried to avoid her and continued to collect resources but when I finally ran into her she wasn't hostile and started talking about the incident the day before.  She talked about how she knew the woman I saved and how grateful her and her family were.
This is the moment this game got me. No hefty reward, no fancy equipment to be gained directly from my action. Just a nice story and praise that a couple of NPCs told me and you know what? It felt great!

A small, fun game that doesn't take itself too seriously. Very fast-paced gameplay behaving like a top down bullet hell shooter. Your goal is simple. There are several weapons you get to use, drive cars, and even level up and improve some of your stats.
The art style is simplistic, but very charming. It looks like scribbled drawings of a small kid, which is a nice and unique style I've not seen before. To complement that, one of my favourite things about the game is how all the sound effects in it seem to be done with voices. The music is pretty nice and light-hearted too.
The game can get a tad repetitive, so it's mostly fun in short bursts, but considering the mechanics and the aesthetics are executed nicely and the game is very cheap, I can definitely recommend it.

Paradigm shifting is a neat way to control your characters in battle, but it should have been a little more mandatory in the first few hours to make it more interesting. Characters are very bland compared to other Final Fantasies but the story otherwise reminds me of FFX. Sounds and music is still great, as expected from Square.
Overall I'd say this is a game you should buy if you're looking for a non-standard JRPG and you're willing to overlook the problems it has. Otherwise, save your money.

As you've no doubt read, Blind Squirrel didn't bother to fix some of the glaring problems with the original PC release. Basically what this means is that you'll have to muck around in the ini files a bit to get proper mouse control and FOV.
Despite the original release receiving a patch to address some of the issues, Bioshock 1 on PC has pretty much always required manual modification to be playable. Frankly, it's extremely disappointing that the developers didn't fix the mechanical issues of such a landmark game - but the good news is that you can easily find 10 years worth of support threads to fix these issues relatively quickly.
The positive side of this release is that the graphical upgrades, though minor, do make an appreciable difference. Most textures look crisper, the character models look much better, the lighting is improved, and the contrast and saturation looks to have been cranked up. Best of all, the upgrade removed the gross "glossy" look that affected half the objects in the original game. The director commentary reels are great.
Overall, this is an excellent oppurtunity to experience the game again - provided you're willing to put in some work tinkering with configuration files.

Review after update:
I played this game on the console a while ago.  I was kinda disappointed when it first got ported to the PC.  I have a high-end PC and was expecting some improvements.  I searched some forums and put in my complaints - for once SE listened.
I waited to play this until the DEC 11th update and I am very pleased.  On max settings, the PC version of this game makes the best console version look like the original Mario...almost no exageration.  I can't say enough good things about how it looks.  They made many improvements and it all flows great.  Although my PC is high-end (to me anyway), it isn't a $2k beast.  I run a 4770k with a gtx770 and I get no lag on max settings.  It only uses 1 core that I can see, so even if you have an i5 it shouldn't make a difference.
If you haven't played it - the game was a great addition to the Final Fantasy series.  Everyone has their favorites, mine were FF9 and FF10, but this wasn't a disappointment by any means.  Unlike most Final Fantasys, this game rushes into the story and uses language that will take some getting used to.  It won't take long for you to catch up.  I'd say within a few hours into the game I knew what was going on.  Another few hours later you can't stop playing.  Worth grabbing it on the PC whether you've already played through it or not.  Hope this helps.

Let's get one thing straight: this is no basic Smash clone. This game is something special. Do yourself a favor, and don't bother reading this review. Just play the game, Schneebly!
But for those of you who don't trust vague suggestions from random strangers on the internet:
I have never been huge on fighting games. I loved Smash, but in moderation. I have also dabbled in Marvel vs Capcom, MUGEN, Skull Girls, and some others. This game single-handedly piqued my interest in the competetive fighting game scene. I followed this game for at least a year, tracking its development. Within the first day of playing Early Access, I was hooked on studying the strategy, getting to know the characters, and learning the ins-and-outs of how to beat the tar out of my friends.
The game is amazingly deep and strategically complex for a 2D brawler, and I am hooked. I spent the better part of yesterday playing with my friend, just battling 1v1 over and over and over. We barely changed characters in between.
Graphics: Awesome pixel art. Super reminiscent of my favorite SNES games, but somehow prettier. 9/10
Animation: Gorgeous. Smooth. Hits are satisfying, motion is believable, characters have weight, playing looks and feels perfect. 10/10
Controls: Simple, but lots of possibilities therein. Control mapping is totally customizable. Characters are responsive, feels great. 10/10
Gameplay: Addicting. So, so addicting. Will be a perfect 10 after the release of more gamemodes, but in EA, it easily gets a 9/10
Features: So much strategy. Characters are incredibly unique and have the COOLEST movesets I've ever seen in a fighting game. As a zoning character, Orcane alone blew my mind, Kragg is my personal favorite, but each character has such a uniqe, creative, impressive, amazingly tactical moveset that greatly caters to their individual strengths and weaknesses. Zetterburn feels a bit overpowered at times, but overall the characters are very well evenly matched in the hands of capable players.  10/10
BUY IT!! Support the developers of this amazing indie game. I cannot stress enough, if you have ANY interest in fighting games, you will LOVE Rivals of Aether. Strongly reccomended.

After impulsively buying and playing this game, It looks like it has the potential to becoming an excellent ♥♥♥♥ing game.
In its simplest form, Salt throws you into a water abundant world full of scattered islands inhabited by Pirates and various Flora and Fauna. You'll find yourself darting island to island Gathering, Looting and Killing to upgrade your Tools, Weapons and Armor. The game does get somewhat repettitive (from what ive played of the game) but grinding up to cool new weapons and rare armor works as a neat incentive.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Positives: 1: Sailing. Big boat or small, manning a ship and sailing it island to island is amazing. Not to mention sprinting
and jumping off your ships deck onto an island and charging into a pirate camp with your ship full
mast, sailing into the distance, is even more amazing.
2: Customisable Ships. With smaller ships you can throw some torches for extra light, or storage crates. For
bigger ships you can put up weapon plaques, chests, fire pits and even a bed.
3: Armor/Tools/Weapons. There are an expansive variety of different armors, tools and weapons, all with
different uses and buffs to suit what you want. Most noticable are armor set
bonuses that can give out extra sailing or movment speeds.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Negatives: 1: 'Boat Menu'. As you work throught the game there are several different vessels you can craft, however
when you eventually craft a boat its saved to your 'Boat Menu'. After that, they pretty much
work as summonable mounts, useable at any time. Allthough its not a major issue, I feel like it
breaks the immersion of the game.
2: No death penalty. From what i've seen, theres no real death penalty with a regular playthrough and with
the mentioned Boat Menu theres no real detterant to staying alive.  There is a Hardcore
setting for this game, so for now it has some optional difficulty curve.
3:Bottomless Inventory. Once again, as far as i've played there is no restrictions to how many items you can
carry. Besides the point of having too much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t clogging up your inventory,
the storage crates and chests and not much use.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Expectations: 1: Misc Customisation. I would love to be able to stick down flagposts with a sigil and colors that i've
picked out to represent my character, More of a finished product thing, but would
still be great.
2: Additional Fauna: Im enjoying hunting down deer with my bow and arrow, though it would be nice to see
some other smaller or larger game to hunt.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Almost all my points are subject to change at this point in time, but I strongly urge people to give it a go. Its not too bad
for $15.00 and it will be great to see some of the additions and alterations they make in later patches.

The first thing you'll notice when playing Salt is how beautiful the islands and water are (if playing with max graphics, at least). Light is the focal point for the majority of the impressive visuals, with shadows not only playing an important aesthetic role but also playing a minor practical role in allowing you to see which direction you're facing while in the middle of a forest without being able to see the sun itself, seeing an animal's shadow before you actually see the animal itself, etc. The game environment simply looks awesome. However, I took two points off because of the minecraft-esque pirates and other blocky models of objects within the environment.

I find the music to evoke emotions of hope, exploration, and/or mystery. It's very appropriate for the type of game and I actually enjoy finding deep ocean because of the music. However, there simply isn't enough scenarios in the game where developers find music appropriate. You won't hear music for much of the game, but when you do you'll be asking why there isn't more.
The sounds are on the right track, but need some more TLC (add more "scary" ones that play under certain specific conditions). There's one sound in the game that (from my experience) tends to play when you're running through the jungle at night. It's a loud "HHWWWOOOOSH" in a high pitch that sounds like some sort of shade attacking. Maybe it's supposed to be an owl or something, but it makes me jump every time. On one occasion I shot an arrow into the shadows of a tree I heard it from, and shortly after laughing at myself for it I turned away to look at a deer down the beach. Right at that time my character's head made a "thunk" sound and my character's vision went down as if hit in the back of the head, temporarily turning my vision downward. I turned all around and nothing was anywhere near me. WTF. I left the island and camped on a nearby one until sunrise.
You are a person that wakes up on a tropical island with nothing but the bare essentials. On your person is a journal left by someone else that tried waking you. This is how your journey begins, and as far as character backstory or finding the person that left the journal, I can't speak to that since I haven't come across either. I didn't rate this since it's an exploration sandbox adventure game with an anonymous protagonist. There's only so much you can do with story in a game like this. Open-ended is just better in general for this type of game.

The gameplay reminds me heavily of classic Everquest. Not necessarily the combat, story, or any other aspects that make a game an MMORPG, but the first-person perspective, the blocky character models, and the large expanse of water and oceans reminds me of the old boat routes, only now you can sail your own boat. I think my review is skewed because of my nostalgia for that game, so keep that in mind.
Combat is mostly just left click, right click to block if it makes sense with the weapon (otherwise hold left click down to do special attacks), and manage your health with buffs/bandages/potions. The accurate trajectories the developers put into arrow paths makes bows easily the most fun weapon you can obtain. At least there's some skill in that.
The sailing in the game is intuitive if you understand rudders, and you'll pick it up quickly enough if you don't. They make it so you can't lose your boats, which is nice, but I think they also coddle players. The game itself seems pretty easy after you get over the hump of not initially being able to find food easily. However, I've never ran out of food and I heard it doesn't do anything but prevent stamina regeneration (also similar to EQ!). There is a huge aspect of the survival game that eventually gets thrown to the wayside after about five hours or so once you stockpile food.
Overall the gameplay is very much what I expected, but they should put more on-use items in the game, or add some way to spice up combat/cartography/whatever. The game just needs new things to do. A lack of bugs and smooth gameplay keeps this rating from dropping lower.
I have mixed feelings about Salt. I think at its core it's a really good game with a lot of potential. The basic premise pulls you in, and the graphics and immersion that they provide with the environmental sounds and lightplay create a really beautiful sandbox.
The problem therein lies that this game is part adventure/RPG and part sandbox. There is some semblance of progression, but never pressure to actually progress. Progression also seems to fall off after a time, though I haven't explored more than a 20x20 grid to the southeast of origin. This doesn't sound like much if you've only play the game a little bit or not at all, but it's actually a huge time investment to clear an area of ocean and take note of the islands and what's on them. In fact, it can sometimes be a little tedious. I've also sailed a straight southern bearing for 40 grid markers to corroborate some of the info in the wiki.
What I'd like to see is an in-game system of cartography so that I don't have to use coffee-stained grid paper for my map. Additionally, I think the game needs to explore its adventure/RPG side a bit more and come up with an overall storyline for the world that players can figure out over time, exploration, and an inquisitive nature. There should be pirate clans that war with one another. There should be islands with dungeons related to the ruins you find around the world. These things should be introduced in the same way that all things in Salt are introduced: through exploration. The story and hard content simply needs to be there for players to find. The worst thing they could do is simply focus on allowing players to collect decorative items for their ships...
Salt is a very clean game that has a lot of potential. I really hope they'll consider adding more content to up the replay-value of the game. Right now I'm not sure there's enough content in the game to keep me playing past 24 hours. For a sandbox adventure explorer I would expect a much higher replay value. It's strange that in a game that's 95% composed of gently-rolling water could be so engaging to explore. Maybe it's because so little of what you can do is documented in-game; you're constantly looking for more materials to combine to see what else you can craft - because the crafting books don't tell you everything. Or maybe it's when you realize that you can get enough equipment to be a fearsome anti-pirate. Or maybe it's just how damn pretty the game is.
I found myself jotting down sextant coordinates of interesting treasure caches, merchants, or ruins. On actual paper. And using those notes to double-back at a later time to profit. Normally, I'd say that any game that forces you out-of-game to "jot down notes" is a failure. But for some reason Salt makes it work. It's refreshing not to have some kind of minimap and HUD. It's a relief to actually fight with the controls of your boat, rather than it just being a speedier version of walking. It's satisfying to plow full-speed onto a beach, hear the grind as your hull skips onto the ground, jump off of the bow and feel like the conqueror of some little patch of land.
In any event, it scratches the itch for an explore-combat-craft game without dropping itself into any major tropes, and making the "explore" part more than "walking simulator".

Hitman: Absolution
+ Good stealth gameplay for the most part, true to the series. Use silenced weapons, your signature fiber wire to strangle enemies or slip past quietly, remaining undetected. Of course, there's always the choice to go in guns blazing as well.
+ Quite a few missions with varied environments, from apartments to small towns and desert areas. This keeps the game interesting.
+ Contracts mode where you can compete with friends, or try your hand at custom assassinations that other players have set up for you to play.
+ Nice graphics.
+ Around 30-35 hours of gameplay for singleplayer.
- You can't choose which guns you want to begin a mission with, which is a big complaint from many fans. There is no customisation, you just begin with the weapons you're given.
- Like previous installments, guards will become suspicious when they see you. There's a new feature called instinct, which allows you to temporarily blend in and become inconspicuous. The problem with this is that you have a very limited amount of instinct and it doesn't recharge during a mission.
- The storyline is quite different to the previous games, it feels odd and unwelcome. There are no assassination tasks per se, but you will still kill high profile individuals. It's a more linear and urgent storyline than usual, with less freedom than its predecessor, Hitman: Blood Money. Agent 47 is being hunted by his own employers and needs to protect a young girl that Diana (his handler) asked him to take care of. He must uncover the truth about why she is so valuable and eliminate those who seek her out.
Overall Score: 7.5/10

Well, looks like I was wrong about this game as a whole. I went into a mini rant about the state of video games and this game was undeserving of it. See, I'm a bit of a purist when it comes to operating systems; I like Windows 7, the base Windows 7, no updates. I played for about and hour and was pretty impressed with the whole setup. The interface is tons better than Duels 2015, which was so slow you might fall asleep between menu transitions. It's still obvious the interface is more designed for tablets, not for PC, but it's fine and there's little to no hanging between the transitions, which is a improvement from last year.
You have to play through the first chapter of the game to unlock the game completely, but for newcomers to Magic, it seems like it does an OK job of explaining things, but I've been playing Magic almost religiously for the past two years, so I didn't need a refresher course about anything. Just play through the tutorials, do the matches, and you get some gold. There's absolutely no catches in this game, you get gold, you use the gold to buy booster packs, and you unlock cards. You don't have to spend a dime. I've already got a pretty decent enough deck going without shelling out a penny. Bottom line, this game is completely free and completely fair.
The sound system is a little buggy at the moment, with some sound effects being way louder than the other sound effects, so much so I jumped a few times when the worst ones played, but it's fine, I'm sure they're already working on it. I've been playing the Duels series since 2013, but I never played with the background music on, I just always felt it broke my concentration. The downside to having the music off though is that the cutscenes become muted too. All the other sound effects are nice and crisp, no complaints about anything else anyway.
Deck building is completely hindrance free. You have the option of composing a deck on your own, how you want it, and if you have the card, you can put it into the deck. Simple.
Haven't tried Two-Headed Giant yet, but from what I've read, it's a little handicapped as compared to Magic 2014. I read that there are no lobbies for multiplayer games, which makes it hard/impossible to set up a completely customized game, I assume that means you can't play with a friend against AI decks either, which is disappointing because my girlfriend and I don't like the pressure of playing against real people. I hope lobbies is something Wizards adds as time goes on, if not, well, we'll either get used to it, or continue playing Duels 2014 for our 2HG fix. All in all, I'm glad the mode is back.
Finally, the graphics are pretty nice looking this year. The battlefield reminds me more of Duels 2014, and I'm glad that they dealt away with the awful pure white battlefield from Duels 2015, that whole game really strained my eyes, but Origins is much better. The artwork on the cards are beautiful as always, MTG art looks great anywhere though. I'm not particularly thrilled about the cutscene graphics however, as I saw someone else say, and completely agree with, it looks like the cutscenes are from 1998 and not something you'd see in 2015, but hey, the game isn't about fancy cutscenes anyway, it's about the game and how it's presented, and the presentation is great.
Despite my problems with the game and needing system updates to actually play it, I think the updates were worth it just to play. It's a good experience for any MTG fan, and a great platform for newcomers to enter the fray. I had exactly one run in with the "lost connection" prompt in the hour I was playing, but it was for barely a couple seconds and the retry button got me back to my game where I won and got some quick gold. I'm guessing server functionality depends on where you live, but I have no idea. I'm glad I was able to resolve the issues and play the game, I didn't want to miss out on it anymore. It's a great MTG simulation, and it's totally free. What more could you ask? I'd definitely recommend this game now.

The Civilization community is toxic. Why? I honestly don't know. By any objective measure, the series is wildly popular. Yet the stunning negativity surrounding Civilization V ("when I first played Vanilla I threw up in my mouth") has transferred itself to Beyond Earth, and the results aren't pretty.
I have had a TON of fun playing Beyond Earth so far. That's VERIFIED fun, people. There IS fun in there. Does the game need polish and balancing? Oh yeah. It's a rushed release, and if you're used to the fine polish of Civ V's UI, many years and expansions along, you'll miss some of that in Beyond Earth.
It has a bunch of bog-standard launch-day UI and balance issues that will be gone in a month or two, but this is an unbearable injustice to today's gamer-on-the-go, apparently.
Here are some of my favorite things about this cool spinoff of Civ V:
1. Finally -- finally! -- espionage is fun in a Civilization game! Really fun! You can spy with flagrant abandon, just like in real life, and diplomatic consequences are rare, just like in real life. Everyone plays the Great Game and nobody pretends spying is just for meanies. The rewards of spying are excellent, and there's little micromanagement. It's a blast!
2. Internal trade routes are a thing! Not a stupid thing, where you move three food from Town A to Town B and somehow that's worth your time. Now, internal routes generate production and food, and external routes generate cash and science. By tweaking routes, you can specialize your economy and adapt to circumstances. Woo!
3. Adaptability! You can change your colony's focus on the fly. The flexibility in the tech tree, trade routes, and espionage missions lets you steer the ship of state with a surprising degree of responsiveness to events on the ground. Strategic resources are of paramount importance. There are a lot of interesting decisions to make, both early and late game. Yay!
4. The theme is awesome and the technobabble is pleasantly passable. It's not just dumb sci-fantasy, and it operates at a much higher level of plausibility than (your favorite pop culture space franchise). It's not hard sci-fi but I'm glad of that.
Here are some things that need work -- and that I think absolutely WILL be improved as the game matures:
1. The combat AI is bad. Is it worse than in Civ V? I don't think so. But Firaxis remains unable to craft an AI that can handle its complicated playing board. If you play Beyond Earth as Space Hitler, you're going to win, and win hard. If you play for the peaceful victories, using war as a tool to hobble your opponents but not gobble them up into the 30th Reich, you will find much more challenge.
2. The UI needs polish. You have to navigate to a lot of screens manually where you ought to just be able to click on notifications. You have to reassign trade routes constantly. It's all a little clicky. May I be the first to say, "Big whoop?" It'll get cleaner, and it's not bad now.
3. Leaders change in appearance as you progress in the Affinities (Purity, Harmony, Supremacy), but you can't see your OWN leader, so you never get to see your OWN cybernetic implants! This is obviously a critical and game-breaking issue. I understand if you do not buy the game because of this.
4. Lots of balancing is needed. Most quests give you false choices, not real ones; if you take +2 Energy from your Autoplant instead of an extra trade route (worth 10-15 Energy and 10-15 Science), you are a pervert. This will get fixed, too, by Firaxis or the community. In the meantime? Pick the right answer and carry on.
Okay... this has been a bit of a ramble. All I want to impress on people is that this is a FUN and DIFFERENT take on Civilization. It uses the same engine and concepts, but it is nothing like a "mod," or a "reskin," and people who use these words to describe it are wrong people whose words are bad.
And, guys? I played Alpha Centauri at release. I loved Alpha Centauri! But it hasn't aged so well. It's a super neat game, but Firaxis has pushed the state of the art in 4X games far beyond that point. When I see someone launch into a diatribe against Beyond Earth by proclaiming their love for Alpha Centauri -- a game with a thousand times more warts and considerably less complexity and variety -- it makes me think, "Now THERE'S a person who would hate the crap out of Alpha Centauri if it were released today."
8.5/10. An innovative spinoff/sidequel of Civilization V with a large new possibility space to explore. Tons of superficial flaws that will probably get fixed. An AI that can't beat Space Hitler, so if you're Space Hitler, expect to zoom "Reich" to victory! Bought twice, once for myself and once for my spouse, and would buy twice again.

If you enjoyed Alpha Centuri (or Civilization 5) then when you play this game you will be sorely disappointed.
The game has so many problems both large and small that learning to play the game takes patience, lots of it! But Ice-T says its good and he should know, he read it on Kotaku!
But look past that and you have a solid 4x war game! Simple in how it functions but deep in how you manipulate it.
You only have a small selection of troop types and as you might expect the game uses a rock papers scissors approach. Ranged can attack safely and enough of them can pick apart melee, however melee can take and deal a lot of damage if it can get close enough and then cavalry (which in this game is jeeps) can quickly chase down archers and pillage enemy tile improvements.
Then you start going deep into affinities and the special units come into play and things get even better.
You will notice I mention nothing else about the game and if you have seen the flurry of Civ:BE reviews you will find many of them point out the flaws, which is easy to do because the game has a lot of flaws! The fact it feels like a reskinned Civ5 is something it never really shakes off either and playing it as if it was an earlier Civ game will leave you sorely disappointed.
What Civ:BE does do right however is take the combat from Civ5 and really improve upon it. War in Civ5 was never really its strong point where as in Civ:BE you can wage chemical warfare, spraying poisonous miasma all over their lands, you can pillage trade routes just like you could in Civ5 however unlike in Civ5 it will really cripple a nation if you can raid enough of them. Speaking of which trade routes automatically stop now during a declaration of war whereas in Civ5 they would just automatically be plundered.
You can launch satellites like the Planet Carver which is as powerful as it's namesake, easily one shotting enemy units and cities! Satellites in general are a fantastic addition to the game, creating an additional layer to prevent a grid locked war.
Supremacy affinity can obtain (cost)free roads, giving them unrivaled manuverability as you can coat the whole map in roads making a rapid response possibly but maybe that sounds too tedious? Well you can launch satellites that will instantly teleport your army!
Hovering units like Hover tanks means you can now press your offensive without having to stop because 'that city is blocked by a hill and ocean'.
The tech web lets you choose how to focus your war effort because while you will want as many techs as possible, you might need a solution to a problem and in Civ5 if you were on the wrong side of the tree at the time, you were so out of luck!
And of course because this is in space we have our 'not-space marines' going up against our 'not-zerg' and I love it! We also have robots but no idea what sci-fi they were taken from, if any.
If you played Civ5 against humans (multiplayer) then you will know that it always comes down to war sooner or later (that great library was mine!) and despite all the bad reviews and stick this game is getting, combat is a huge improvement over previous Civ games. I daresay only Civ2 had combat this engaging (Diplomats?! Fanatics?!) so if you want to play a 4x 'not-warhammer' then certainly get a copy of this game for you and a friend!
Sadly the AI is brain dead. I won't mention the other flaws but you cannot play this game, even on its hardest setting and actually get a challenge from the AI so either go online or play with a local friend and have a blast. For those who prefer single player then

Before I get into this review I'd like to adress a situation with AC3.
AC3 followed the story of Revelations where it ended off, Desmond woke up from his coma and was off to another new adventure.
In AC3 you overall got also introduced to a new Assassin Connor which most people call him uninteresting or lacking in terms of what Ezio had in store for you, but you shouldn't really put much blame on AC3 because of the Assassin design and what his atitude was in general.
Connor in my honest opinion was a brutal as hell Assassin, a loving and caring person when it came to his natural enviormeant the Village and the Homestead, but a literall devil on the battlefield, characther design and atitude in general were pretty good and didn't lack in anything if you understood the point of his characther overall.
AC3 overall was a pretty great game can't be top tier like AC2 or BF but it was a pretty great game in general.
Now for BF.
BF is either Great, Terific, Amazing, Glorious or God tier. It's pretty much an undescribable game for me really I enjoyed the hell out of it as a fan of the franchise for a long time, the overall core gameplay of it was smooth and fast paced and it was just an adrenaline rush in its own ways.
The game offered us a better and more extende Naval Combat system which we have been asking for from AC3 and its probably the most fun you could also have in the game, the game in general is mainly covered 60% sea and 40% land making the Naval Combat one of the more important aspects of the game.
The Naval Combat in BF is far superiour than what other Pirate/Ship battle games have and its quite alot of fun to just destroy the hell out of some giant fleets.
Now overall the story and characther of the game.
In BF the story picks off some time latter from AC3.
Overall your characther is unknown as he is some kind of employe working for Abstergo as a double agent of some sorts since you technicaly share intel with the Assassins troughout the game in the modern day missions of the game ( Shaun and Rebeca ) overall the modern day segments are covered in a first person perspective and are just a bit odd, fun but odd, the fun thing you could really have in the modern day segments is just randomly collecting some QR codes and hacking PC's, yes hacking is a thing in this game, the hacking is pretty fun altough it repeats the same short minigame of either switching frequencies, turning a line from point A to point B in order to unlock the file or just a simple cracking the firewall type of game, pretty short but they are also pretty fun in general.
The story of BF takes before the actions of AC3 so that means your way behind playing as the grandfather of Connor Kenway.
Captain Edward James Kenway or as people called him that started off as a privateer at the begining of the game, overtaken for the lust of having a better life, greed is his main priority he takes as he pleases and doesn't give a rotten damn about anything, but hey thats the usual which you expect from a pirate, but troughout the game thinking that he may be some bad characther he overall isn't, he did get a bad reputation with both secret organizations but overtime learnt the morals of which had taken him quite some time to understand, over that course he sought to fight along side the Creed and follow its morals. He also was technicaly the founder and Grand Master of the English Assassin's Brotherhood. He grew to be quite a likeable characther in my opinion atleast.
The core gameplay of it is as same as it was in AC3 with a few difrent changes to fit the playstyle of a pirate, duel wielding cutlasses and owning 4 flintlock pistols is the deal with AC4, the naval combat also has been improved from AC3 and also making it the main thing in the game.
The game adds another important characther to it the Jackdaw which is your ship that you sail trough the Caribeans plundering and taking as you want, it's important that you take of your ship as it becomes quite the game changer if you upgrade it to max and all.
Overall the game is good it'll take you aroudn 20-23h to complete that is if you spend next to no time on the naval contratcs, templar hunts, assassin contracts and such oh yeah and upgrading your ship which will take you quite a while to find the parts as there also a new mechanic added to game called Treasure hunting, you can find treasure maps from dead or unconcious corpses stranded on the shores of the locations you discover, each treasure map will containt either gold or an upgraded plan for the jackdaw and some aditional gold, sure gota love that pirate feel afterwards.
Anyways got a bit offtrack there.
The game at its base is great and all has a very small amount of glitches ( exclude the sinken rising ship thing which ocasionaly happens with the Jackdaw ) and so fort.
The gameplay is great and is just amazing in some sense as you feel like a genuine pirate with the tools at your disposal.
A much recommended game and also a favourite in my category as it just captures everything you could need in an AC game.

Let's start off by saying that I'm a big fan of the casual indie genre. I'm not sure how this game managed to not get a casual tag, but it definitely deserves one. You're literally just walking around a forest as a badger with little badger pups. Not a whole lot else going on.

Overview: A fun addition to the AC franchise. All the AC gameplay you like (sneaking, fighting, climbing, jumping) with the added bonuses of being a pirate with your own ship.
Good
+ Solid Assassin gameplay from other games. It is mixed up a little to fit the time, but if you love AC games you'll fit right in.
+ Pirate ship! The ship gameplay is solid and fun. You get the feel of a ship on the seas without the tedium. A mix of speeds and fast travel help with life on the high seas. The ship battles are fun and fierce. Deal with waves and wind and cannon arcs but with plenty of help to keep it exciting. Choose to capture or sink ships as you will.
+ Good story. You take a good story arc as your character grows from a simple man with a simple plan to a master assassin caught up in a worldly struggle.
+ Manage your own fleet. It is a side game of its own, but very profitable if you stick it out.
Bad
- The 'offline' animus story is mediocre at best. Not near as fun as being a pirate.
Overall a fun game.

For anyone a fan of the Civilization series, you will thoroughly enjoy this title. It is set up like any other civ game, from a small settlement to a sprawling empire. However there are a lot of noticable differences from the normal civ formula that bring the user a refreshing change to the game. It is not a simple reskin of civ v as some suggest, it is its own game. However the game is plagued by multiplayer issues as, civ v is also, so you might want to hold off on buying it until they come out with a patch.

I enjoyed Shelter for what it was;  A casual survival game with a message about life to convey.  However, I cannot commend it for the story alone.  Clocking it at almost exactly 45 minutes, Shelter is remarkably short.  Despite the game being so short, it introduces a lot of gameplay variations, only to discard each one.  By the middle of the game, I had forgotten to butt trees for apples because there were so many ways to gather food.  Survival is hardly a struggle, just a happening in this game.  Fun mechanics, like the night level and river crossing, were discarded not 15 minutes after they were introduced.  The final level introduces nothing new, just the same easy Hawk-dodge mechanic from early in the game.  The game is also stuck between the "do-it-yourself" school of gaming and the "please-hold-my-hand" brand of tutorial-based gameplay.  (The only challenge in the game is figuring out how to feed your baby in your den.  Everything else is given an instructional pop-up lesson.)  A fine message and an interesting artstyle, not worth the price of admission.

I have logged hundreds of hours on Civilization V, and have all the DLC. Many reveiws complain that this game is unfinished and unbalanced. Having played less than a hundred hours, I can honestly not yet comment on the balance. However, the game has a lot of content presently, and is wholly a different game from any of its predecessors, including Alpha Centauri. What seem like simple decisions and directions can turn out to be quite complex. No longer does one have to wait until end-game to enjoy things like spy agencies, planes or artillery, all are less than 2 techs away. You are forced to adapt based on your surroundings: No xenomass? Better rethink becoming a harmony civ. Franco-Iberia just built the promised land gateway? Better refocus on military and destroy it before they finish the victory condition. All in all, an enjoyable and independent sequel to the Civilization V mechanics.

This is not what you would consider a normal game. This is the definition of indie, although I'd hesitate to even call it a game. More of an interactive experience than anything else. The goal of Shelter is to guide 5 badger cubs to safety through various different environments as the parent badger, making sure all five are kept safe from predators and well fed. The "game" takes about an hour to complete, but that hour is one emotional rollercoaster. If you have a couple bucks and a little patience Shelter is well worth it. Shelter does a phenomenal job of connecting the player to the badger family he/she is responsible for, especially considering the short completion time.  With the right mind set going into this game it is excellent. I definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for something to chew on after they've finished.

Rivals of Aether takes a lot of inspiration from the Super Smash Brothers titles (namely Melee), and adds its own unique twist to it. The combat is very unorthodox, even compared to the already unorthodox Smash Bros series, with each character being able to control the stage in their own ways.
If you are a fan of Smash but find the formula starting to become a little bland, then pick up this game. Just be aware that since it's still in early access there could be a few bugs, but of my (almost) 20 hours of playing it, I haven't run into anything game breaking. Online matchmaking is a bit finnicky at times, with some matches lagging more than others, but I've had hardly any problems playing with friends.
If you're looking to get into smash, or have no other alternative, then I'd definitely pick up Rivals of Aether. It's a great game with a lot of similar aspects to Nintendo's hit brawler franchise, and there's no better alternative than this.
I'll actually be a little envious of Xbox One owners when this game hits the Arcade.
Final thoughts: Great game, interesting gameplay, awesome characters and movesets. Online is a little iffy at the moment, and there are some bugs, but those will probably all be ironed out as Early Access nears its completion.
